concerns: Rodent intranasal efficacy papers support biological rationale but do not evidence EV-specific, membrane-protected mechanism — the proposal correctly treats this as unproven, but the project risk remains high until the spike-in/orthogonal assays are validated (supported by ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution provides direct contradictory translational evidence for intranasal delivery in a large species; the proposal notes this but must explicitly plan experiments to distinguish administration/formulation/labeling failure from true absence of EV exposure.

Key methodological assumptions (assay sensitivity/specificity; lack of detergent/protease artifacts; spike-in tracer behavior) are not supported by the provided canonical evidence and represent critical single points of failure for the design.

The proposal labels inference edges as indirect_support and inference appropriately; ensure that any affirmative claims about EV-association remain conditional until the proposed orthogonal in vivo->ex vivo bridge is experimentally demonstrated (avoid treating rodent efficacy as proof of EV-specific mechanism).

Manufacturability and regulatory implications are sensibly tied to outcomes, but the proposal should avoid implying that MISEV2023 mandates a specific potency gate—MISEV offers guidance supporting rigorous orthogonal characterization but does not itself define regulatory potency criteria.
conclusion: The proposal is generally consistent with the supplied canonical evidence: rodent intranasal efficacy reports (ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus, ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi, ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome) support pursuing mechanistic linkage experiments but do not demonstrate EV-specific, membrane-protected activity in vivo; MISEV2023 (ev-misev2023-quality-framework) supports orthogonal, spike-in-controlled approaches; and a non-human-primate negative biodistribution study (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution) correctly flags delivery/translational risk. The proposal appropriately frames key inferences as requiring additional experiments and does not misattribute literature results as internal (SGL-001) experimental outcomes.
evidence_gap: Several operational assumptions in the proposal lack direct support in the supplied canonical evidence: (1) that available capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation have sufficient sensitivity/specificity for low-biomass nasal-lavage/CSF samples; (2) that detergent + protease/RNase treatment reliably distinguishes membrane-protected cargo from artifactual signal in the proposed matrices without introducing assay artifacts; (3) feasibility and in vivo detectability of an exogenous orthogonal intact-EV spike-in tracer in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue samples; and (4) that linking orthogonal in vivo recovery to ex vivo microglial cytokine modulation is achievable across lots and species. These are explicit experimental gaps to be addressed by the proposed work.
